facts.fact: The African Union Commission's status list of 02/02/2026 shows Burundi with no date of signature, ratification/accession or deposit for the Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection (21 signatures and 20 deposits across 55 states).

facts.fact: Participants in the Paradigm Initiative and Dukingire Isi Yacu workshop in Bujumbura on 18-19 February 2026 called on the Government of Burundi to ratify the Malabo Convention, which the article treats as not yet ratified.

The article says experts at the February 2026 workshop found gaps and non-compliance with the Malabo Convention in Burundi's new personal data protection law (adopted 15 January 2026, promulgated 10 March 2026) and in the 2022 cybercrime law, although a government delegate described the data law as aligned with regional and international standards.

note: Names the Malabo Convention and the Protocol on Digital Trade only as relevant continental frameworks; states nothing on Burundi's signature, ratification or national law under them.

Concerns the EAC Statistics Bureau Bill, a shared statistics law that is not digital, so class other; no signature, ratification, national digital law or cross-border application of African digital law is stated.
The Malabo Convention is cited as a norm the strategy respects; no signature or ratification is stated.
The document states nothing for this study about the country.

facts.fact: Gako News reports a workshop asking the President to sign and ratify the Malabo Convention, which Burundi has neither signed nor ratified.
Burundi deposited instruments of ratification of the ATU Constitution and Convention at ATU headquarters in Nairobi, the ATU says.
